name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development-Anorectal Anomalies Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XX DSD-Anorectal Anomalies Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with discordant phenotypic sex
Congenital anorectal anomalies such as imperforate anus or rectovaginal fistula
Ambiguous external genitalia including clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion
Abnormal steroid hormone profiles consistent with androgen excess
Pelvic ultrasound or MRI showing internal female reproductive structures with anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with discordant phenotypic sex plus at least one major criterion of anorectal malformation and ambiguous genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, endocrinology, and pediatric surgery.

laboratory: Abnormal steroid hormone profiles consistent with 21-hydroxylase deficiency or other enzymatic defects
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI showing internal female reproductive organs with malformations
genetic: Possible mutations in genes involved in steroidogenesis or sex differentiation (e.g., CYP21A2)
other: Clinical examination revealing ambiguous genitalia and anorectal anomalies
Multidisciplinary assessment including endocrinology, genetics, and pediatric surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Typically 46,XX with androgen excess but without anorectal malformations
Different pattern of genital ambiguity and absence of anorectal anomalies

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia with inability to identify sex at birth
Imperforate anus or inability to pass stool
Recurrent urinary tract infections indicating urogenital malformations
references: Orphanet: 46,XX difference of sex development-anorectal anomalies syndrome - ORPHA:2973
